SOURCES / HOW THIS WORKS

Real imagery. Clear distinctions.

Map pulses follow the scheduled My mix notes using the audio output clock. Each pulse follows modeled distance over travel time and highlights B at the delayed arrival. Original and paths without a return have no arrival animation.

Atmosphere overlay

Visual source

Current selection

Video time refers to the imagery. The atmosphere grid is a separate historical MERRA-2 sample from 1 January 2025.

Ocean surface

NASA SVS · Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature. NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio; ECCO2 model. Full 68.6-second animation at 1200 × 600 and 30 fps. All source video frames retained without re-encoding; original audio omitted. Blue to red represents cooler to warmer surface water, not sound pitch or current speed. Ocean model period: 25 March 2007–3 March 2008. Playback time is compressed animation time, not elapsed real-world time. The ~ month/year label estimates model time by mapping playback progress across this published date range. NASA’s frame-date table has 2,001 entries while this mirrored movie has 2,059 frames; exact frame-to-date alignment has not been verified.

Aerosols

NASA SVS · GEOS Aerosols. NASA GMAO / SVS; Joseph V. Ardizzone and Helen-Nicole Kostis, scientific consulting Lesley Ott. Animation covers 1 August–14 September 2024. The full unlabelled 2:1 animation uses the 1920 × 960, 30 fps Wikimedia video directly, without further downscaling or re-encoding. Downloaded from a Wikimedia mirror of the NASA video, labelled public domain (PD-NASA). Blue/cyan: sea salt; pink/magenta: dust; red/orange: smoke; green: sulfate. These represent particle types, not temperature or altitude. No motion is fabricated. Replaces the earlier 19 August 2025 still; the dates differ.

Region surfaces and waveform

Region cards crop the selected bounds from the actual NASA video. Surface height is display brightness: (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B) / 255, on the same 0–1 scale for every card. A sampled grid is drawn in perspective with the source colors. This is an artistic brightness relief, not terrain, physical altitude, temperature, or aerosol concentration. Coordinates are approximate image coordinates. Cards from the same dataset share its video clock; paused video produces a stationary surface. Single-region playback uses the active region; node playback uses the selected nodes. The waveform reads the audio output after effects and volume, with an automatically scaled, labelled amplitude axis and time in milliseconds; it is not a recording of Earth. Atmospheric profiles are independent historical data, not simultaneous measurements of the image.

Data & calculations

Estimated travel time before speeding up the audio: —. Playback uses this time divided by 1,000.

Air temperature—Wind along this direction—Sound speed including wind—

Wind + means with the sound; − means against it. Values describe the starting point.

Temperature and wind charts show how the air changes with height. These are not audio waveforms.

Horizontally uniform, flat-Earth ray model. No absorption, horizontal weather changes, or loudness prediction. The audible delay is artistic time compression, not a validated simulation of bells propagating through the atmosphere.

Thermal-layer methods

Xian & Homeyer (2019): lapse-rate tropopause method · Dubé et al. (2026): stratopause temperature maximum · NASA: atmospheric layers. Our sampled-level estimates do not reproduce the satellite study’s spline retrieval.

Region surfaces

Brightness controls surface height on a shared 0–1 scale. These surfaces represent image brightness, not physical elevation.

Node melody

Melody mode assigns composed notes and beat lengths to region nodes. Current video colors control timbre and loudness; neutral strips remain silent. The notes are not inferred from NASA data. The Template selector offers Sweden or a named melody you create. Named templates save notes, beat lengths, region assignments and tempo in this browser, and edits save automatically. Instrument, Sound Lab settings, Echo and scan speed remain separate. Tempo is independent of scan speed. Each sounding note uses its own region’s atmospheric path and the same compressed delay for audio and animation. Repeat nodes repeats the score; otherwise it plays once. The built-in short, melody-only phrase from Sweden by C418 / Daniel Rosenfeld is adapted from a publisher sheet-music preview. This is a locally synthesized excerpt, not the full song or an embedded recording. Save frame mix exports a frame sonification, not this composed score.

Regional sound

Bells use a rounded strike and fading upper tones; soft synth uses gentle harmonics and a slower attack. Orchestral adds synthesized string and soft brass layers with a light bell accent at the same color-selected pitch. These are synthesized timbres, not recordings of orchestral instruments. All instruments keep the color-selected pitches and scheduled note times, with smooth releases.

Drag a box or click the flat map to capture an image region. A click selects a small surrounding area. Coordinates assume an equirectangular image; rendered-map registration is approximate. Playback scans 16 strips from left to right across the selected region, then repeats. Each step samples the current video frame. Scan speed ranges from 0.5x to 2x: about two to eight strips per second, depending on rendering time. Scan speed saves automatically in this browser. Adjusting it changes future note spacing, not video speed, pitch mapping or atmospheric travel time. The thin line marks the strip producing the current note; color chips show its sampled colors. This is synthesized audio, not a recording of Earth. Pause or seek the imagery to pause or reposition the sonification. Selected regions save automatically in this browser. Listening follows the current video frame. Save frame mix exports a static phrase from the latest sampled frame, not a recording of the full live performance.

Original is now synthesized from the selected image colors, not a fixed example clip. For static playback, sixteen west-to-east columns control a 4.5-second phrase. Live playback reads one column per tone, with a 250 ms sampling interval at 1x, adjusted by Scan speed, plus rendering latency. The scan line uses the scheduled audio output clock; silent uncolored strips advance the scan without launching a sound pulse. Overlapping live notes use a soft saturation stage to bound their summed output. Ocean hue maps cooler-looking blue to lower notes and warmer-looking red to higher notes. Each strip samples 8 by 48 points and keeps five color families separate, so mixed blue and red produce separate notes instead of one average pitch. Within each family, hue sets pitch; brightness and colored coverage affect amplitude. Square-root color weights help smaller patches remain audible, while a shared gain budget bounds the combined level. This remains a sampled, quantized interpretation, not every pixel or color difference. This does not recover numerical sea temperature or current velocity. Aerosol hue bins map visualization categories (sea salt, dust, smoke, sulfate) to four note ranges; brightness is not a measured concentration. Uncolored and very dark pixels are ignored, along with the ocean color-key area. Palette classification is approximate. Bells and soft synth choose timbre; My mix applies EQ, smoothing, dynamics, width, reverb and low-octave controls. No AI generation, model or training is used by this app.

Map pulses follow the scheduled My mix notes using the audio output clock. Each pulse follows modeled distance over travel time and highlights B at the delayed arrival. Original and paths without a return have no arrival animation.

Atmosphere overlay

Map marker A is the nearest atmospheric grid cell used for the selected region. B is the calculated return location, projected along the chosen bearing using the model’s return distance. The dotted line is its ground track, not the elevated sound ray. Labels are offset to avoid overlap; their small dots retain the actual coordinates. No B is shown when the model finds no return.

Atmosphere data marks valid atmospheric profiles in the cached global MERRA-2 grid. Sound returns uses the same ray calculation as Atmosphere details for the selected direction and launch elevation. Teal cells predict a return to the starting height at a distant receiver; gray cells have data but no return within the model limits (highest sampled center below 60 km, maximum range 2,000 km). Hatched cells indicate unavailable profiles. No return does not mean no atmosphere, and does not rule out a return above the sampled heights. The cell boundaries follow nearest-grid selection, including the longitude seam and polar rows. This is a separate historical 1 January 2025 sample, not a live map or simultaneous with either visualization. Overlay colors do not enter the audio or brightness sampling.

Atmospheric travel

The playing region shows audio-timed note journeys inside a transparent atmospheric volume sharing the perspective of its image-brightness relief. The atmosphere path uses that card’s own profile and the selected direction and launch elevation. Each audible note launches a marker on the audio output clock. Its receiver arrival uses the same calculated travel time divided by 1000 as the delayed audio copy. Overlapping notes have separate markers; the receiver flashes on arrivals. Original mode, silent regions and stopped playback do not show delayed arrivals. Browser frame rate and audio-device timing limit visual precision; it does not model a reverse echo. Horizontal path extent is fitted to the image footprint in the selected compass direction; it is not a geographically located receiver. The vertical axis is exaggerated and brightness is not terrain altitude. The atmosphere base is raised above the brightness relief for visibility; dashed anchor lines are visual connectors, not extra sound-path segments. Transparent sheets mark estimated thermal-layer boundaries and the sampled profile top at the same vertical scale as the ray. They are not reflecting surfaces. Temperature and wind are the inputs to the path calculation; detailed values are in Atmosphere details. No return is invented when the path exits the sampled profile or range limit. Pausing, seeking or stopping playback clears scheduled markers along with the notes. Reduced-motion preferences keep the path static while the current-layer readout and receiver cue update.

The animated cross-section uses the selected profile and the existing piecewise-linear effective-speed ray, without forcing a return. The path chart is static; its dot marks the sound’s starting point. The independent height and distance axes exaggerate height. The chart shows the path, starting height and starting layer. Temperature, wind and sound-speed readouts are in Data & calculations. Values are interpolated from the selected profile under the horizontally uniform model assumption. Positive wind is along the chosen direction. Effective speed is sqrt(1.4 × 287.05 × temperature in kelvin) plus along-path wind, calculated at sampled levels and linearly interpolated between them. These changes with height determine the modeled bending; there is no reflective ceiling. Readouts describe the starting point. The map and region-card animations follow audio playback.

The selected region center requests its nearest actual grid cell from NASA MERRA-2, regridded by GEOS-Chem at 4° × 5°. Both region coordinates and cell coordinates are shown. Fields are for 1 January 2025: T, QV and PS interpolated from 00:00 and 03:00 UTC; wind is the 00:00–03:00 mean. The separate path chart shows the calculated ray from that cell. Changing video colors changes the emitted sound; it does not change the independent January 2025 temperature/wind profile. Ocean/aerosol imagery is from different times and sources, not simultaneous atmospheric measurements.

With Echo enabled, My mix includes one modeled delayed arrival when a return is found, with amplitude 0.45 and travel time divided by 1000. Echo off removes this delayed copy and its arrival flash; the modeled path animation remains visible. Echo saves in this browser, independently of scan speed. Changing Echo restarts the current scan or node sequence to clear already rendered delayed notes. Sound Lab reverb is a separate effect. Original has no arrival effect. A source cue and arrival at a distant receiver are combined for presentation; this is not an echo measured at the source. No return is invented when the ray exits the profile or exceeds the model range. The flat, horizontally uniform effective-speed model excludes curvature, terrain, absorption, horizontal weather changes and crosswind advection.

Estimated thermal layers join at sampled-profile boundaries. First tropopause uses the 2 K/km lapse-rate criterion throughout the next 2 km, searching sampled levels from 5–22 km above model surface. Stratopause is an interior temperature maximum in 35–58 km, with cooler temperatures 2 km above and below. No secondary tropopause is identified. The profile ends near 60 km, not at the top of the atmosphere. Unresolved boundaries remain unavailable. Layer labels show estimated profile height ranges above the model surface; the gold readout tracks the moving wave’s current layer and height. A low-opacity gold volume highlights that same layer between its calculated boundaries. Diagnosed layer heights set the translucent sheets in region cards; numerical heights remain in the separate scientific charts. The sheets do not alter the calculated sound path. Imported media is visual-only and has no verified geographic selection.
